newsitem.title: TURKEY: Steel seller in highest bid for Turk bank sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Steel seller in highest bid for Turk bank sell-off.

text.p: A local iron and steel exporter and industrial gas producer gave the highest bid in a tender on Thursday for Turkey's state-owned Anadolubank, officials said.
They said Mehmet Rustu Basaran, owner of the Istanbul-based Habas company, gave $69.5 million for Anadolubank in the open bargaining session held by the Privatisation Administration (OIB) in Ankara.
Its bid is yet to be apporved by the Higher Borad of Privatisation, a body consisting of the prime minister and some other senior ministers.
Basaran's bid outdid its closest follower Zorlu Holding, whose highest bid stood at $69 million.
A total of 12 companies participated in the tender, which opened at $38 million for the bank.
Anadolubank is an offshoot from the state Etibank formed by transferring assets of three Etibank branches -- in Ankara, Istanbul and Izmir.
On Monday, the OIB held a similar tender for Etibank's privatisation in which the local textile producer Dogan Kumascilik gave the highest bid for $185 million.

The government split Etibank in September into three banks -- Etibank, Anadolubank and Denizbank -- to make its sell-off easier. Etibank is one of the key parts in the government's privatisation drive, targeted to raise $5 billion in 1997.
The tender for Denizbank, also formed by assets of three Etibank branches, will be carried out on Friday.
